question: What will be the ending value of the ICE BofA US High Yield Option-Adjusted Spread for these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 7 - Sep 18)

calls.reasoning: Series is highly persistent and sits at 2.65 (2026-09-03), ~5bp off its 52-week low and in the tightest ~5% of 25-year readings. Reference class (10-business-day-ahead levels from a tightest-decile start) gives a near-random-walk median of ~+2bp, so the status-quo outcome dominates: median 2.67. Distribution is right-skewed because the empirical floor (~2.55-2.60, unbreached since 2011) compresses the left tail while the FOMC Sep 15-16 hike (60-66% priced), heavy September AI-driven HY supply, a $9.6tn Sep 18 options expiry and Hormuz oil-supply risk fatten the right. Offsetting that: 162k payrolls vs 53k expected cuts default risk, VIX is 14, and both 2024 and 2025 Sep-3-to-Sep-18 windows tightened 10-17bp. Horizon is only ~9-10 business days and FRED's one-day publication lag means the resolving print is likely the Sep 17 observation. No prediction market prices this contract, so no crowd blend. Evidence is solid on the series itself but thin on forward-looking credit-specific catalysts, so I stay close to the reference-class anchor.

disagreements.claim: Relevant dispersion is the calm-regime SD (~0.085, width 0.22) vs the full-2026 SD (~0.15-0.17, width 0.38-0.44).
disagreements.verdict: Neither. Calm-regime SD understates an event-dense window (CPI, live FOMC, $9.6T opex on the resolution date); full-2026 SD is contaminated by the Feb-Mar widening regime. Reconciled to 0.285.

disagreements.claim: The median should sit above spot (~2.67) because compression room is thin.
disagreements.verdict: Partly rejected. Thin downside room justifies a fat right tail, not a higher center. The index tightened through the hawkish repricing, so drift is neutral; median set at 2.66 with the asymmetry loaded into the upper wing.
